title: WISE 0855-0714

catalog.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7 (J/ApJS/253/7, parallax and motion fit)

catalog_comparison.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7 (J/ApJS/253/7, parallax and motion fit)

spectrum.method: Forced ePSF photometry on native pixels at the motion-corrected (followed) position in every exposure; wavelength from the spectral WCS at that pixel; inverse-variance means in the 102 SPHEREx/SPIFF bins.

fixed_vs_follow.note: Measured at one fixed sky position, the source keeps 58% of the flux recovered by following its motion (median over 15 bins).

templates.library: SPIFF SPHEREx templates (Gagné et al. 2026; M4–Y0 field, low-gravity and subdwarf grids)
templates.reason: Best template Y1 (field) with reduced chi-square 1.32 over 42 bins. Y1 is the coldest template in the library, so the true type may be later (colder): read this as 'at least as cold as Y1', not as a precise type.

naive.description: Every exposure in time order, regardless of wavelength. Because SPHEREx sees a different wavelength in each exposure, most of this apparent change is the source spectrum, not time variability.
naive.max_ratio_basis: brightest / faintest exposure among those with S/N >= 10

matched.description: Flux in the same SPHEREx wavelength bin compared between visits. Only this comparison can reveal true time variability.

hypotheses.name: Stationary astronomical source
evidence: A stationary model is rejected: delta chi-square 91 (about 9 sigma if the per-point errors are realistic).

hypotheses.name: Moving astronomical source
evidence: Proper motion 10066 ± 1062 mas/yr from 12 exposures over 221 days; model reduced chi-square 1.01.

hypotheses.name: Blended or overlapping sources
evidence: 1 Gaia DR3 source(s) within 12 arcsec (2 SPHEREx pixels); nearest 7.1 arcsec, G = 16.3.

hypotheses.name: Instrumental or processing artifact
evidence: Detected in 12 independent exposures across 2 visits, on multiple detectors and wavelengths.

hypotheses.name: Known solar-system object
evidence: Positions over 221 days follow linear proper motion of a few arcsec per year (reduced chi-square 1.01); solar-system bodies move arcseconds to arcminutes per hour and would not repeat a stellar track across visits.
No known asteroid or comet lies within 60 arcsec of the source at any of the 8 observation times checked (IMCCE SkyBoT cone search).

verdicts.label: Known source recovered (Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7)
Spectrum consistent with an ultracool dwarf (Y1)

summary.headline: Moves 10.07″/yr across 12 SPHEREx exposures; spectrum matches a Y1 template.
summary.one_liner: Detected in 12 independent exposures with a coherent position change. The motion-corrected spectrum is consistent with a Y1 template (the coldest template available, so the object may be colder still) (reduced chi-square 1.3), which supports but does not prove an ultracool-dwarf classification. Nearby sources may contribute light within the 6.15-arcsec pixels.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15 arcsec; sources closer than about 1 pixel are measured as one blend.
Positions are registered to Gaia DR3 field stars with a pure shift per exposure; residual distortion is absorbed into an empirical error floor.
Fluxes use the median pixel solid angle (OMEGA_MEDIAN) and the release ePSF; absolute calibration uncertainties of a few percent are not propagated.
Parallax was not fitted (fewer than three visits); the motion is a linear approximation.
A template match constrains spectral type only; it does not establish mass, age or formation history.
Not in Gaia DR3 (too faint in the optical).
NASA brief coordinate 08h55m10.831s -07d14m42.53s is a historical (WISE discovery era) position; PARALLAX propagates the Spitzer-based solution to each SPHEREx epoch instead of searching that spot.
Mass and formation interpretation are model-dependent; PARALLAX does not call it a rogue planet.
follow_up: Check higher-resolution imaging (e.g. unWISE, 2MASS, Gaia) to separate contributors.
Extend the baseline with archival WISE/NEOWISE epochs to tighten proper motion and parallax.
